Evidence:
[1] It is located on the border between New South Wales and the ACT, the NSW portion in Kosciuszko National Park and the ACT portion in Namadgi National Park.
[2] Kosciuszko National Park covers 6900 km2 and contains mainland Australia's highest peak, Mount Kosciuszko, for which it is named, and Cabramurra the highest town in Australia.
[3] Cabramurra was the third highest permanently inhabited town on the Australian continent, situated at 1,488m (only 82m lower than Dinner Plain in Victoria, and 272m lower than Charlotte Pass Village in NSW) AHD (4,880 ft) in the western Snowy Mountains of the Great Dividing Range, in the state of New South Wales.
[4] The track weaves mainly through Australian national parks, such as Alpine National Park and Kosciuszko National Park, though it is not exclusively restricted to national parks.
